audit.corrected: report[14].t reworded to 'Favoured matchup', difficulty left at 6/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 0, 2, 4, 5 and 6 disagreed with the packet chart — the page gave Renekton level 3, first item and two items, and called level 6 Skill.
audit.why: Packet levelChart is Renekton / Renekton / Skill / Skill / K'Sante / Skill / K'Sante. Level 6 belongs to K'Sante because All Out knocks Renekton through a wall for an isolated duel and heals him; two items belongs to K'Sante on the same duel plus tank scaling. The content whys[2], whys[4], whys[5] and whys[6] already say exactly this — only the side tokens disagreed.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 2, 4, 5 and 6 flipped in matched full/content pairs, ratings adjusted, and the four full-layer whys that claimed Renekton pressure at those stages rewritten.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page says Path Maker (W) 'blocks' Renekton's stun in four places, calls the Q a knockup in five, and never mentions the Footwork shield.
audit.why: Riot's text: Path Maker charges up TAKING REDUCED DAMAGE, then dashes and knocks back and stuns — it grants damage reduction, not unstoppable, and it cannot negate Ruthless Predator's stun. Ntofo Strikes damages and SLOWS in a line, and at 2 stacks fires a shockwave that PULLS enemies in — there is no knockup and no third-cast chain; it is a 3.5s cooldown, 20 energy. Footwork (E) is a dash that grants a SHIELD, and a 50-Fury Ruthless Predator destroys damage shields on the target and stuns for 1.5s, which is the decisive interaction and appeared nowhere. All Out heals him, so Grievous Wounds decides the level-6 fight; while All Out, Path Maker no longer knocks back or stuns.
audit.corrected: The 'W blocks the stun' claim removed from whys[1], spikes[0].text, wants.you[0], wants.foe[0] and early; the Q corrected to a 2-stack pull in whys[3], mid, dontsFull[0].d and wants.foe[1]; the Footwork shield-strip stated in wants.you[0], whys[1] and spikes[0].text; anti-heal put in dontsFull[1].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page tracked All Out as the lane cooldown, which is a 120s ultimate the player cannot trade around wave to wave.
audit.why: The cooldowns that actually gate lane trades are Ntofo Strikes at a flat 3.5s and Footwork at 10/9.5/9/8.5/8s — Footwork is the shield-and-dash you have to force out before committing.
audit.corrected: Footwork's 10s cooldown written into phases[2].why and the Path Maker charge tell into dosFull[1].d.

edits.before: Play level 1 short and patient — K'Sante's Q1 poke is awkward to confirm on a moving target, so auto-trade and deny CS without burning E yet. At level 2 you get your spike: E through him, immediately cash empowered W before his W animation can block the stun, then Q for the triple heal — this two-hit burst is your bread and butter for the next three levels. He cannot answer a clean E-W-Q all-in at levels 2 or 3; every trade should start with E so you threaten the dash-through and force him to either burn W preemptively or eat the full stun.
edits.after: Play level 1 short and patient — Ntofo Strikes is a 450-range line that is awkward to confirm on a moving target, so auto-trade and deny CS without burning E yet. At level 2 you get your spike: E through him, immediately cash 50-Fury W — Path Maker's charge only reduces the damage he takes, it never stops the stun — then Q for the heal. He cannot answer a clean E-W-Q all-in at levels 2 or 3; every trade should start with E so you threaten the dash-through and force him to burn Footwork early or eat the full 1.5s stun.

edits.before: Levels 4 and 5 are your control window — bank Fury between trades and force the extended all-in whenever his W cooldown is up. His Q knockup is the main thing to dodge: K'Sante chains Q1-Q2-Q3 to knock you airborne, which breaks your combo if it lands mid-animation, so E in at an angle and stun him before he completes the chain. At level 6 the math flips — his R All Out strips his own resistances and turns him into a mobile fighter with percent-HP damage; do not commit to a solo kill if All Out is available, as he will dash you into a wall, isolate you, and out-duel you in that window.
edits.after: Levels 4 and 5 are your control window — bank Fury between trades and force the all-in whenever Footwork is on its 10s cooldown, because that shield is the only thing that blunts your burst and a 50-Fury W destroys it outright. The Q is a slow, not a knockup: two Ntofo Strikes stacks fire a shockwave that pulls you back in, so step in on the stack he just spent. At level 6 the math flips — All Out knocks you through a wall, heals him and gives him percent-HP damage at the cost of his own resists; do not commit to a solo kill while it is up, because that isolated duel is the fight he wants.

edits.before: Bank 50 fury on the wave, slice onto K'Sante when his answer is down, empowered-W stun + Q heal, and dice out clean.
edits.after: Path Maker charges first and only stuns on release — the charge is your cue to leave its 600-range dash.

edits.before: That is K'Sante's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: Two stacks of Ntofo Strikes fire a shockwave that pulls you straight back in.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: All Out heals him, so bring Grievous Wounds before you fight it.

notes: This page carried the 'Path Maker blocks the stun' myth the mirror flagged, and it was load-bearing: four separate lines told the player his combo would be negated by an ability that only reduces incoming damage while charging. The counter-fact — 50-Fury Ruthless Predator destroys Footwork's shield — was absent from every field. Second live error: Ntofo Strikes was described as a knockup with a Q1-Q2-Q3 chain in five places; Riot's text gives a slow plus a 2-stack shockwave that pulls. Titles under 25 characters (dontsFull[0].t 'Get walled by his Q') still misdescribe the Q, but the applier skips strings that short, so they are reported here rather than proposed.
